subject: gk
question: A small enterprise is one in which investment in plant and machinery does NOT exceed what amount?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs. 10 crore**__.

Source: https://msme.gov.in/know-about-msme

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A small enterprise is defined based on the investment in plant and machinery.
 
• The investment threshold for a small enterprise is Rs. 10 crore.
 
• This classification helps in providing targeted benefits and support to small enterprises.
 
• Small enterprises play a crucial role in the economy by contributing to employment and GDP.
 
• The definition and criteria for small enterprises can vary by country and are often subject to regulatory updates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Micro Enterprises**

 
 
• These are businesses where the investment in plant and machinery does not exceed Rs. 1 crore.
 
• They are the smallest category of enterprises and often operate with a small workforce.
 
 
 
• **Medium Enterprises**
 
 
• These enterprises have an investment in plant and machinery between Rs. 10 crore and Rs. 50 crore.
 
• Medium enterprises are larger than small enterprises but smaller than large enterprises.
 
 
 
• **Government Schemes**
 
 
• Various government schemes are available to support small and medium enterprises, including financial incentives and subsidies.
 
• Examples include the Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) and the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP).
